bib.title: Accurate, Large Minibatch SGD: Training ImageNet in 1 Hour

question: Can synchronous SGD with very large minibatches (up to 8192) train ImageNet ResNet-50 without losing accuracy, and how must the learning rate and early training be handled?
hypothesis: Large-minibatch difficulty is an optimization problem, not a generalization problem; a linear learning-rate scaling rule plus warmup should fix it.
contributions: Hyper-parameter-free linear scaling rule for learning rate vs minibatch size
Practical pitfalls of distributed SGD (weight decay, momentum correction, loss normalisation, shuffling)
Caffe2 system training ResNet-50 with minibatch 8192 on 256 GPUs in one hour at ~90% scaling efficiency
Transfer to COCO detection/segmentation with Mask R-CNN

method.summary: Distributed synchronous momentum SGD on ResNet-50/ImageNet with lr = 0.1*kn/256 and a 5-epoch linear warmup from 0.1, keeping all other hyper-parameters fixed. Minibatch sizes 64 to 64k are compared over 5 runs each, plus ResNet-101, ImageNet-5k and Mask R-CNN transfer, with an allreduce implementation (Gloo) on Big Basin servers.

datasets.name: ImageNet-1k
datasets.preprocessing: scale and aspect ratio augmentation as in fb.resnet.torch; 224x224 random crop or horizontal flip; per-colour mean/std normalisation

datasets.name: ImageNet-5k
datasets.size: 6.8 million images (4k extra categories from ImageNet-22k)
datasets.split: 1k-way error on original ImageNet-1k validation set

models.name: ResNet-50 (fb.resnet.torch variant, stride-2 on 3x3 layers)
models.init_from: from scratch; He et al. 2015 init for convs, FC weights zero-mean Gaussian std 0.01, BN gamma=1 except last BN of each residual block gamma=0

models.name: Mask R-CNN
models.init_from: ImageNet-pretrained ResNet-50 at each minibatch size

training.objective: cross-entropy classification loss plus L2 weight decay
training.optimizer: Nesterov momentum SGD, m=0.9 (standard momentum equally effective)
training.lr_schedule: reference lr divided by 10 at epochs 30, 60 and 80
training.warmup: gradual: start at 0.1, increase linearly each iteration to kn-scaled lr over 5 epochs (results robust to duration)
training.batch_size: kn = k workers x n=32 per worker; 8192 main (256 GPUs); 64 to 65536 swept
training.weight_decay: 0.0001, not applied to BN gamma and beta
training.regularisation: BN statistics computed per worker with n=32, running average momentum 0.9
training.hardware: Big Basin servers, 8 NVIDIA Tesla P100 GPUs each with NVLink, 3.2TB NVMe, Mellanox ConnectX-4 50Gbit Ethernet; 256 GPUs for 8k, up to 352 GPUs in timing
training.wall_clock: 1 hour for ResNet-50 at kn=8k on 256 GPUs; 92.5 minutes for ResNet-101 at 8k on 256 P100; baseline 29 hours on 8 P100
training.seeds: 5 independent runs per config; error = median of final 5 epochs, mean and std over runs

other.large batch simulation: kn>=12k simulated on a single server with gradient accumulation (footnote 5)
other.reduction: allreduce: NCCL intra-server for buffers >=256KB, halving/doubling inter-server (3x faster than ring on 32 servers), Gloo library
other.data shuffling: one random shuffle per epoch partitioned over k workers
other.Mask R-CNN: per GPU 2 images, 512 RoIs per image; 5 pretrained models per size, 35 models total

parameters.linear scaling rule: multiply lr by k when minibatch is multiplied by k

limits: Evidence is ResNet-50/101 on ImageNet with SGD momentum; batch-size limit (~8k) is empirical and depends on setup
Beyond about 8k accuracy degrades and training diverges beyond 64k with linear scaling
Results at 8k are more sensitive to lr than at 256; authors suggest staying away from the breaking point
Very large (>=12k) batches were simulated with gradient accumulation, not distributed
Linear scaling rule justified only informally; assumes gradient changes little over k steps
Optimization difficulty claimed rather than generalization problem 'at least on ImageNet'
5x larger dataset does not change the maximum effective batch
No cost in dollars or total FLOPs given

terms.definition: When the minibatch size is multiplied by k, multiply the learning rate by k.
start from a learning rate of η and increment it by a constant amount at each iteration such that it reaches η̂ = kη after 5 epochs
scale v by the factor ηt+1/ηt when the learning rate changes in the variant that absorbs η into the update tensor
